subject: Renewal & expansion: proposal for term restructure and commit increase
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@sierrahealth.org>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal discussion + additional capacity questions

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the continued partnership — Sierra's clinical search pilot has been solid and our product team wants to expand usage into two additional regions next year. We're coming up on our contract renewal in January and have a few asks from procurement: a multi-month price hold if we increase committed capacity, consideration for a one-time operational credit to offset migration work, and clarity on how unused committed units are handled.

High level: right now we expect to increase committed spend by ~30% if we can get a short price guarantee (90 days) while our migration finishes. Can you outline options and any flexibility on discounts/credits for a 12–24 month renewal?

Thanks,
Alicia Gomez
Head of Platform Integrations
Sierra Health Systems

---
Attachment: migration_plan_outline.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@sierrahealth.org>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion + additional capacity questions

Hi Alicia — really glad to hear the pilot is scaling and that you're planning expansion. High-level options we can offer for your renewal window: 

- 12-month renewal with a 10% net seat/usage discount off list for the renewed committed spend.
- One-time operational credit to offset migration (we can discuss $15k–$30k range).
- 90-day price hold for any incrementally committed spend above your current baseline (prorated).
- Rollover credits: unused committed units convert to service credit valid for 90 days after term end (we can change this in a contra addendum).

I'll loop in Pricing and Finance to craft a formal proposal with numbers. If agreeable, we can prepare an addendum and DocuSign packet for procurement. Are you able to share a target commit figure so we can run exact pricing?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0128

Subject: Fwd: Renewal discussion + additional capacity questions — pricing ask

Team — forwarding Alicia's ask. Key points: +30% committed increase target, requests: 90-day price hold on the incremental commit, and a one-time migration/operational credit. Procurement will need SOC2 links and the DocuSign flow.

Can we run 2 scenarios:
1) 12-month term: 10% discount on renewed commit + $20k operational credit + 90-day hold on incremental commit
2) 24-month term: 15% discount on renewed commit + $25k credit + 6-month hold for the incremental capacity

Please see attached worksheet for numbers — I need an approved range to present. If Finance is comfortable with the credit and hold, we'll propose scenario 2 as preferred (locks in longer term).

Thanks,
Hannah

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-23T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal discussion + additional capacity questions — pricing ask

Hannah / Connor — reviewed the worksheet and ran impact on ARR. My recommended commercial packaging: 

- Preferred: 24-month renewal, 15% off list on committed spend, minimum 30% commit increase. One-time $25,000 operational credit applied at kick-off. 6-month price hold on incremental commit.
- Alternative: 12-month renewal, 12% off list, $15,000 credit, 90-day hold on incremental commit.

Rationale: 24-month with the higher credit and longer hold materially improves retention risk and gives Redwood predictability; it also reduces churn and preserves margin with the commit increase. Finance (Vivek) — please confirm tolerance for $25k credit and wording on prorated refunds vs service credit for unused committed units.

I also recommend adding an explicit addendum clause that unused committed tokens roll into Redwood service credits for 180 days (not cash refunds) to protect revenue while giving the customer runway.

—Marissa
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-24T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Proposal: Sierra Health renewal — term options and next steps

Hi Alicia / David — thanks for the details. Per our internal review we've prepared two options for Sierra's renewal. Attaching a short addendum with the preferred commercial terms. Summary below: 

Option A (Preferred) — 24-month renewal
- 15% discount on committed spend (applies to the renewed baseline + incremental commit)
- Minimum 30% increase to committed spend compared to current baseline
- One-time operational credit: $25,000 applied at contract effective date
- Price hold: 6 months on any incremental commit above baseline
- Unused committed units convert to Redwood service credit valid for 180 days (no cash refunds)

Option B — 12-month renewal
- 12% discount on committed spend
- $15,000 operational credit
- 90-day price hold on incremental commit
- Unused committed units convert to service credit valid for 90 days

Next steps: if Option A looks good to Procurement, we will:
1) Finalize addendum and route DocuSign (link below)
2) Provide SOC2 evidence folder and security attestation (Drive link below)
3) Finance to prepare billing schedule and revised invoice template

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.net/contract/SHS-2026-REV
SOC2 & security evidence: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aSierraHealth-SOC2-evidence

Please let me know which option Procurement prefers and I'll send the addendum for signature. Happy to jump on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
